programme: NKX2-1 (TTF1) as lineage-identity anchor versus ZNF281 as a dedifferentiation/stemness driver: NKX2-1 sits on and maintains a follicular/neuroendocrine identity programme (TG, TPO, CALCA, RET, TTF1 itself), while ZNF281 reaches into NANOG and VIM, the canonical stemness/EMT pair, plus ODC1 — the opposite pole of the same axis, reprogramming a differentiated cell toward a proliferative, dedifferentiated state.
role_in_a: In Stroke, ZNF281 surfaces as an immune/vascular-injury biomarker in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (36172261) — consistent with a dedifferentiation-type stress response in injured vessel wall or reactive glia. NKX2-1's placement is weaker and indirect: 38916623 is about the germline NKX2-1 'brain-lung-thyroid' syndrome (chorea, hypotonia, congenital hypothyroidism) discussed as a differential diagnosis for Huntington's disease — a neurodevelopmental movement disorder, not adult ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke.
role_in_b: In Thyroid_Cancer, NKX2-1 is the master follicular-lineage transcription factor, and its chromosomal locus (14q13.3) is an established GWAS susceptibility region for thyroid cancer (19198613). ZNF281 is reported as a super-enhancer-associated transcription factor rewiring glucose metabolism specifically in poorly-differentiated thyroid carcinoma (36121916) — the dedifferentiated end of the disease spectrum, where NKX2-1-driven identity is characteristically lost.
shared_axis: If a tissue loses its NKX2-1-anchored lineage programme and gains a ZNF281-driven stemness/EMT programme, the resulting phenotype — dedifferentiated, proliferative, metabolically reprogrammed — is the same cellular logic whether the tissue is a thyroid follicular cell turning into poorly-differentiated carcinoma or a vessel-wall/glial cell reacting to hemorrhagic injury; the pairing rests on this shared identity-loss logic rather than on any stated clinical or anatomical link between the two diseases.
reasoning: The module is nameable (identity-maintenance TF vs. dedifferentiation TF) and each pole is independently anchored to Thyroid_Cancer by good evidence (a GWAS locus and a mechanistic super-enhancer/metabolism study). But the Stroke side is thin: NKX2-1's paper is about a genetic movement-disorder syndrome, not ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke as usually defined, and ZNF281's stroke evidence is a single biomarker paper with no mechanism shown. No paper here connects the two diseases through these factors, so this is a plausible-but-undocumented reach rather than an established or independently-supported axis.
support: 38916623 — NKX2-1 germline mutation causes brain-lung-thyroid syndrome with chorea and hypothyroidism, discussed for neurological differential diagnosis (weak stroke relevance, real thyroid relevance); 19198613 — GWAS locus 14q13.3 (NKX2-1) associated with thyroid cancer susceptibility; 36172261 — ZNF281 identified as a key gene in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage; 36121916 — ZNF281 is a super-enhancer-associated TF regulating glucose metabolism in poorly-differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
how_to_falsify: Stain or qPCR matched tissue pairs — acute hemorrhagic/ischemic stroke vascular or perilesional tissue versus well- vs poorly-differentiated thyroid tumor sections — for NKX2-1 and ZNF281/NANOG/VIM. The account predicts a reciprocal shift (ZNF281/NANOG/VIM up, NKX2-1 and its targets TG/TPO/CALCA down) co-occurring in both the dedifferentiated thyroid tumor and the injured stroke tissue; if stroke tissue shows no such reciprocal shift (e.g. ZNF281 rises without any NKX2-1 change, or NKX2-1 is simply undetectable/irrelevant in vascular tissue), the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|thyroid, meaning the Stroke network itself is built from blood, not brain or vessel-wall tissue directly — the mechanistic papers cited for the stroke-associated factors (including the higher-recurrence ones below) come from separate brain/vascular experimental models, not from this blood-derived network. 69 patient-group comparisons were available, but NKX2-1 (38/69) and ZNF281 (36/69) are mid-pack, not top-recurring: ZFHX3 (51/69), ZFP64 (47/69), TFAP2C (45/69) and RBPJ (38/69) have much stronger, more mechanistic stroke evidence (pericyte contractility, Notch-vascular remodeling, cerebral-infarction GWAS) but zero documented thyroid-cancer connection in the retrieved papers — that better-supported vascular/Notch-pericyte programme is real but disease-specific to Stroke, and is not the axis reported here. None of the excluded single-view or tissue-generic factors bear on this account, so their removal is not masking an alternative story.
